title: Webb County leaders align priorities ahead of 2027 Texas legislative session
excerpt: Webb County Judge Tano Tijerina and State Rep. Richard Peña Raymond met to align county and state priorities before the 90th Legislature opens Jan. 13, 2027, with water, colonias and border-port infrastructure at the top of the list.
content:
Webb County Judge Tano Tijerina and State Representative Richard Peña Raymond met this week to align county and state priorities ahead of the next Texas legislative session, the 90th Legislature, which begins Jan. 13, 2027, according to KGNS.

The two leaders discussed infrastructure, economic development, water, colonias, education and health care, KGNS reported. Both said they have a productive working relationship and meet regularly to talk through the county’s needs.

Water was a central topic. Raymond said the Legislature approved about $3 billion for water infrastructure statewide, while noting that Webb County and South Texas still face water-supply needs, according to KGNS. He said the county should bring its projects forward so he can work to bring funding back to Webb County, and Tijerina said the county should communicate its needs directly and not be afraid to ask the state for help.

Colonias were also a central focus. Tijerina said he was elected largely to work on colonias and described growing up without running water or wastewater service, KGNS reported. Webb County is seeking about $4 million for colonia water, wastewater and roads, and Raymond noted that colonias are a top priority for Tijerina.

Raymond, who has served in the Texas House since 2000, filed 150 pieces of legislation in the 89th session, with 100 of those passing, according to KGNS. Border ports of entry infrastructure and economic development were also among the priorities the two discussed.

Education and health care were listed among the broader priorities, though no specific proposals were detailed, KGNS reported.

Source: KGNS, Nov. 12, 2026.
